result_title: Environmental and social drivers of urban garden biodiversity: a PRISMA-ScR review
summary: This scoping review synthesizes 30 studies on how environmental conditions and gardeners’ social and management choices shape biodiversity in urban gardens. Larger, structurally diverse gardens with varied plants and connections to natural habitats often support more species, while intensive maintenance and pesticide use can harm biodiversity; the authors note geographic and taxonomic gaps and call for integrated, inclusive garden planning and further research.

The USDA Climate Hubs page describes urban agriculture—from community gardens and rooftop farms to indoor growing—as a way to supplement local food supplies and support climate resilience. It can shorten food supply chains and emissions, store carbon, reduce urban heat, improve food access and biodiversity, and strengthen community education, though land costs and limited city guidance can hinder its growth.
